text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"No privacy or generative AI review recorded","detail":"The proposal uses an LLM (generative AI) and drivers' GPS location history (personal data) to draft performance warnings that affect driver standing. It records only 'Ops leadership supports the pilot', not any privacy, legal, or AI governance review.","evidence_quote":"Ops leadership supports the pilot.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and document privacy/data protection, legal/HR, and generative AI policy reviews before the pilot. Cover the use of location data, human review of drafts, and driver recourse."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days of standard and design mismatch","detail":"The plan runs 4 weeks, which meets the minimum, but the success target is set at 12 weeks. A 4-week test cannot validate a 12-week target. Randomizing by market with no stated number of markets also makes the power claim unsupported, since market-level clustering is not accounted for.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by market. Duration: 4 weeks. MDE: 0.3 incidents per 10,000 trips, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Align experiment duration with the 12-week target window, or restate the target for 4 weeks. Report the number of markets and a cluster-adjusted power calculation."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"Missing guardrails for driver impact and warning quality","detail":"The change affects driver discipline and pay-adjacent outcomes, but the only guardrail is earnings. There are no guardrails for driver attrition or churn, warning accuracy and error rate (LLM hallucination), delivery completion or on-time rate, or driver appeals and disputes.","evidence_quote":"Driver Hourly Earnings: must not fall below baseline.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails for driver attrition, share of warnings overturned or edited by managers, appeal and dispute rate, and delivery quality metrics."},{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"Time-savings problem claim lacks quantification and verifiable source","detail":"The claim that managers spend 'hours' drafting warnings is attributed to an ops time study with no figures or link. The problem's size cannot be verified, and the proposal never defines a metric for time saved.","evidence_quote":"Operations managers spend hours drafting warnings to drivers with repeated service issues (source: LMD ops time study).","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the study with specific figures, such as average minutes per warning and volume. Add a success metric for manager time saved."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Success metric does not logically connect to the intervention","detail":"The intervention drafts warning letters, but the success metric is Driver Safety Incident Rate. Nothing links the drafting of warnings to the safety rate, and the stated problem (manager time) is not measured. The metric's mapping to the intervention is unclear.","evidence_quote":"Driver Safety Incident Rate: baseline 3.1 per 10,000 trips, target 2.6 within 12 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Define a primary metric tied to the problem, such as manager drafting time per warning. Keep safety incident rate as a secondary or guardrail metric, with a stated causal rationale."}]}
